purpose: P0-S2 evidence batch: AT-red-white-red process, AU-skilled financial-requirement and process, CH-study eligibility/financial-requirement/process.
policy: Only exact route claims supported by current official sources are included. Promotion requires complete material-field coverage at high confidence.

records.claim: Red-White-Red Card applications are submitted to the competent Austrian authority (Magistrat or Bezirkshauptmannschaft) in Austria, or to the Austrian representation abroad for applicants outside Austria. The employer and applicant must jointly satisfy the applicable category criteria; the card is issued for 24 months and entitles the holder to take up employment with the sponsoring employer. A Red-White-Red Card Plus may be applied for after 24 months of qualifying employment.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Austrian federal Red-White-Red Card application process guidance.

records.claim: Australia's skilled migration programme operates through the SkillSelect system. Applicants submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) and, if invited, lodge a visa application within 60 days. The programme includes points-tested streams (subclass 189, 190, 491) and employer-sponsored streams. Invitations are issued in periodic rounds based on points score and occupation demand.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Department of Home Affairs SkillSelect and skilled migration programme guidance.

records.claim: Australia's skilled visa streams do not publish a single universal proof-of-funds threshold applicable to all subclasses. Financial requirements are subclass-specific: subclass 189 has no published universal proof-of-funds requirement in current Department of Home Affairs guidance; subclass 190 and 491 requirements are state/territory-nominated and vary. This record documents the absence of a universal financial threshold rather than asserting one.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Department of Home Affairs skilled migration programme overview. No universal proof-of-funds figure is asserted; subclass-specific financial requirements must be verified per exact subroute.

records.claim: Third-country nationals wishing to study in Switzerland must obtain a residence permit for the purpose of study. Applicants must be enrolled or accepted at a recognised Swiss educational institution, demonstrate sufficient financial means for the duration of study, and satisfy the general conditions for entry and residence in Switzerland.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swiss federal study residence permit guidance for third-country nationals.

records.claim: Switzerland requires study-permit applicants to demonstrate sufficient financial means to cover tuition fees and living costs for the duration of their studies without recourse to public funds. The applicable threshold is assessed by the cantonal authority and is not published as a single national figure; applicants must demonstrate self-sufficiency for the full study period.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swiss federal study residence permit financial-means guidance. No unsupported universal figure is asserted.

records.claim: Third-country nationals applying for a Swiss study residence permit must apply at the cantonal migration authority of the canton where the institution is located. Applicants outside Switzerland apply through the Swiss representation in their country of residence. The permit is issued for the duration of the study programme and must be renewed annually. A letter of acceptance from the institution and proof of financial means are required.
records.methodology: Direct review of current Swiss federal study residence permit application process guidance.
